links.outcome: Discrimination of candidate ML models versus traditional logistic regression for early postoperative infection
links.effect: XGBoost had the highest AUROC, 0.96 (95% CI 0.93-0.98), and was chosen over the other ML models and the logistic regression comparator; Brier score 0.02.
links.quote: The XGBoost model achieved the highest performance with an AUROC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.93-0.98).

links.outcome: ICU stay, hospital costs and antibiotic use density with model-guided versus empirical antibiotic upgrade
links.effect: The model-guided group had lower AUD (P<0.01), shorter ICU stay (median 5 vs 6 days, P=0.01) and lower costs (median ¥150,000 vs ¥200,000, P=0.01). The matched comparison was retrospective, not randomized.
links.quote: According to the XGBoost model, the DEICS group significantly demonstrated reduced AUD ( P < 0.01) in the matched cohort, along with decreased ICU stay time (median: 5 vs. 6 days, P = 0.01) and hospital costs (median: ¥150 000 vs. median: ¥200 000, P = 0.01) in the EPI cohort.

screen.reason: The study deployed a machine learning model across four centers and compared clinical outcomes (antibiotic density, ICU length of stay, costs) between patients whose antibiotic treatment followed the model's recommendations versus standard empirical care.

primary.practice: AI-guided antibiotic escalation vs empirical care
